cases.title: First lesson on Mentor Practice: Title, its pairs, leave-outs, a frame, then the read-the-graph step

rubric.reason: Turn 1 proposes only Title and names its pairs by property and time from the snapshot ('three Position moves (0.5 to 1.5 s, 1.5 to 3 s, and 3 to 4.37 s) and a Scale move from 0.5 to 1.5 s'), and says 'which you eased in your easing lesson'.

Turn 1 covers every left_out kind with one short line each ('You've hidden Old Take', 'CTRL is a null', 'I can't see inside Icon yet', 'An expression drives Logo's Rotation', and the ease-first pairs). It never calls a precomp fine or a layer expression-free, and asks the land-hard question once.

Turn 2 asks the learner to open the Graph Editor, choose Edit Speed Graph, and say where Position 0.5 to 1.5 s is fastest (start, middle, end). Turn 3 takes a frame at 1 s inside that pair and explains influence in plain words (longer landing handle, shorter start handle) with no numbers and no claim to see the graph.

Every name and time the mentor uses appears in the snapshot or the learner record: Title, its Position and Scale times (4.37 rounds 4.367), Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness, and Title in eased_layers.

Turn 1 proposes only Title ("which you eased in your easing lesson") and names its four pairs by property and time from the snapshot (Position 0.5–1.5 s, 1.5–3 s, 3–4.37 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s), without listing other layers' candidates.

Turn 1 gives one short sentence for each kind listed: hidden Old Take, null CTRL, "I can't see inside Icon yet", "An expression drives Logo's Rotation", and the ease-first pairs; it never calls a precomp fine and asks once "Should any of Title's moves land hard?"

Turn 2 asks the learner to open the Graph Editor, choose Edit Speed Graph and say whether Position 0.5–1.5 s is fastest near the start, middle or end; Turn 3 takes a frame at 1 s inside that pair and explains influence in plain words (longer ease into the landing key, shorter out of the start key) with no influence or speed numbers and no claim to see the graph.

Every name and time the mentor mentions appears in the snapshot or the learner's record: Title, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo Rotation, Subtitle Opacity, Bar X Position, Glow Blurriness, and pair times 0.5/1.5/3/4.37 s (4.37 is 4.367 rounded); "you eased Title" matches eased_layers.

Turn 1 proposes only Title, notes it is 'the layer you eased in the easing lesson', and names its four pairs by property and time from the snapshot: Position 0.5 to 1.5 s, 1.5 to 3 s and 3 to 4.37 s, plus Scale 0.5 to 1.5 s.

Turn 1 gives each left_out kind its own short line (hidden Old Take, null CTRL, 'I can't see inside Icon yet', 'An expression drives Logo's Rotation', and Subtitle/Bar/Glow still needing easing), never calls a precomp fine or claims there is no expression, and asks once whether any of Title's moves should land hard.

Turn 2 has the learner open the Graph Editor, choose Edit Speed Graph and say where Position 0.5 to 1.5 s is fastest (start, middle or end); Turn 3 takes a frame at 1 s inside that pair and explains influence in plain words with no numbers (longer ease on the landing key, shorter on the start key), without claiming to see the graph.

Every name and time the mentor uses (Title, Position, Scale, 0.5/1.5/3/4.37 s rounded from 4.367, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness) appears in the snapshot result, and 'you eased' Title matches eased_layers in the record.
